title: Ranveer Singh Wrote a ₹10 Crore Cheque to Leave Don 3. The Industry Can't Stop Talking About It.
excerpt: CINTAA president Poonam Dhillon says 'kudos' as Bollywood's messiest contract dispute turns into a masterclass in how to exit gracefully — if you can afford it.
body:
In Bollywood, walking out of a project is gossip. Walking out and paying for it? That's a power move.

Ranveer Singh's exit from Don 3 — the Farhan Akhtar-directed reboot that would have cemented his place in one of Hindi cinema's most iconic franchises — has been the industry's most whispered-about saga for months. But the latest developments have turned whispers into open admiration, at least from some very powerful corners.

Poonam Dhillon, the veteran actress and president of CINTAA (Cine and TV Artistes' Association), went on record this week with a word rarely used in Bollywood power disputes: "Kudos."

"Kudos to him that he offered compensation for losses incurred and paid back the signing amount. Many don't even do that." — Poonam Dhillon, speaking to Free Press Journal

The Numbers Behind the Exit

Here's what happened, stripped of the industry euphemisms: In December 2025, three weeks before international shoots were scheduled to begin, Ranveer formally departed from Don 3, a project he had been attached to since its announcement in August 2023. The reason cited, depending on which source you trust: creative differences, an unlocked script, and what Ranveer's camp has described as a fundamental disagreement over the film's direction.

The financial fallout was real. Excel Entertainment — the production house run by Farhan Akhtar and Ritesh Sidhwani — reportedly sought approximately ₹40-45 crore in damages, covering pre-production costs, location bookings, crew commitments and scheduling disruptions that cascaded across their entire slate.

Ranveer's response? He returned his signing amount in full, offered ₹10 crore in direct compensation, and — in a move that reads like something out of a corporate negotiation playbook — reportedly offered a ₹25 crore discount on his fee for any future collaboration with Excel. That last part is the detail that has people talking. It's not just a peace offering. It's a relationship preservation strategy wrapped in a financial gesture.

The FWICE Drama

Things got uglier before they got better. The Federation of Western India Cine Employees (FWICE) — a powerful body representing below-the-line workers — issued a non-cooperation directive against Ranveer, effectively threatening to make him unhireable. The directive sent shockwaves through an industry that has seen plenty of disputes but rarely formal action against its biggest stars.

CINTAA, which represents actors specifically, pushed back. Dhillon made it clear that her organization stood with Ranveer while encouraging an amicable resolution.

"As an actor, he has the right to select his work, and it is between him and the producer how they handle the matter. He's responsible and committed to his work, and we have seen his body of work." — Poonam Dhillon, speaking to Variety India

The directive was eventually withdrawn after dialogue between the parties. But the fact that it was ever issued at all has reopened conversations about the power dynamics between stars, producers and industry bodies — conversations that Bollywood usually prefers to have behind closed doors.

The Family Angle

In a revealing detail, Dhillon shared that she had been in direct communication with Ranveer's father, Jagjit Singh Bhavnani, throughout the dispute. "I spoke to Ranveer's father at length, and we have been corresponding on WhatsApp. He has thanked me for our support," she told Variety India.

According to Dhillon, the elder Bhavnani clarified that despite the dispute, there was "no animosity" toward Farhan Akhtar or the Excel team. "He's given two big hits with them," Dhillon noted, referencing Ranveer's earlier collaborations with Excel on Dil Dhadakne Do and the National Award-winning Gully Boy. "If there was any reason he is not comfortable doing this film, could be for various reasons."

Translation: it wasn't personal. It was professional. And in Bollywood, where professional and personal are often indistinguishable, that distinction matters enormously.

What Happens to Don?

The franchise isn't dead — just orphaned. With Ranveer out and no replacement announced, Don 3 sits in limbo. Farhan Akhtar's next moves will determine whether the franchise finds a new face or quietly folds. Meanwhile, Ranveer is channelling his energy into Pralay, a ₹300 crore survival thriller being billed as one of Hindi cinema's most ambitious action projects in years — the kind of film you commit to when you're done playing someone else's legacy character.

For the NRI watching this unfold from Houston or Harrow, the takeaway isn't really about which film Ranveer does next. It's about what the Don 3 saga reveals about modern Bollywood: even the biggest stars have to negotiate their way out, the money is always bigger than the headlines suggest, and sometimes the most professional thing you can do is write a very expensive cheque and walk away with your reputation intact.

Don 3 remains uncast. Ranveer Singh begins shooting Pralay in August 2026.
